u01-rem-close.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. Ps 29 (30):3-4, Luke 22:29 (Καὶ ἐγὼ διατίθεμαι ὑμῖν διαθήκην), Habakkuk 2:3 (Ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονιεῖ), 1 Cor 15:16 and Mark 12:7 (Δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν) are correct identifications of the quoted texts, given in parentheses as apparatus. 'Christ's resurrection would not have been that cause' renders the elliptical conditional εἰ γὰρ μὴ τὸ τέλος … ἡ Χριστοῦ ἀνάστασις; the English supplies the implied apodosis without changing the argument. 'I may not be pierced with sorrow' stands for οὐ μὴ κατανυγῶ in a purpose clause. 'Such was the wonder of the bush' (οἷον ἦν), 'non-resisting' (μὴ ἀμυνομένους), 'they will hear God accomplish' and the μέν/δέ and relative-pronoun points are matters of style.

u01-rem-close.resolution: I found no meaning error. Luke 22:29 and Habakkuk 2:3 are the actual sources of the quoted words; the edition's Ps 39 headings are lemma headings, not citations of these words. The elliptical εἰ γὰρ μὴ τὸ τέλος … clause is rendered with its implied apodosis. In 'seeks for himself the mercy upon them that comes to us', εἰς ἡμᾶς qualifies the mercy and ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ goes with 'seeks', which is exactly what the English says.
